sentences.text: Petitioner's case 2.The case of the petitioner is that he was aged 12 years and pursuing VII - Standard at the time of accident.

On October 9, 2014, at about 05.00 p.m., while he was returning home from School, a Bus bearing Registration No.TN-32-N-2076, belonging to the respondent / Transport Corporation was stationed at Chavadi Bus Stop.
When the petitioner attempted to board the Bus through the front door, the Driver of the Bus, without adhering to the rules, moved the Bus.

Due to this negligent act,
the petitioner fell down and back wheel of the Bus ran over both the petitioner's legs.
Thereby, the petitioner suffered grievous injuries to his left thigh bone, third toe on the right foot, hip, chest and multiple other injuries all over his body.
2.1.Immediately, the petitioner was taken to Government https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2344 OF 2022 Hospital, Kurinjipadi, where he obtained treatment.
Then, on the same day, he was referred to Government Headquarters Hospital, Cuddalore, where he received further treatment.
Later, on October 10, 2014, he was shifted to Mahatma Gandhi Medical College and Research Institute, and was discharged on October 20, 2014.

entities.text: Mahatma Gandhi Medical College and Research Institute
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Even after being discharged from the hospital, the petitioner continued treatment as an out-patient in Private Hospitals.

Due to the accident, the petitioner suffered injuries and fractures to his left thigh bone and third toe on the right foot rendering him unable to stand for long periods, walk, squat or sit cross-legged.
He is unable to perform any work independently.
Therefore, the petitioner seeks a total compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondent under various heads including attender charges and future medical expenses.
Respondent's case 3.The respondent filed a counter stating that the bus driver of the respondent / Transport Corporation followed all the rules and regulations while driving the bus.

When the bus driver stopped at Kurinchipadi Chavadi Bus Stop, the plaintiff tried to board the bus carelessly, attempting to secure a https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2344 OF 2022 seat in the crowd, and ended up falling on the step in the midst of the pushing and shoving.
The said accident was not caused by the respondent Bus Driver.
Accordingly, it prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
4.At trial, the petitioner was examined as P.W.1 and Ex-P.1 to Ex-P.7 were marked on the side of the petitioner.
On the side of the respondent, neither witnesses were examined nor documents were marked.
Disability Certificate of the petitioner was marked as Ex-C.1.

Findings of the Tribunal 5.The Tribunal after considering the materials and evidence, concluded that the Driver of the respondent's Bus is responsible for the accident and held that the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Relying on Ex-C.1 - Disability Certificate which shows 21%
permanent disablement and Ex-P.3 - Discharge Summary, the Tribunal concluded that the petitioner suffered 21% partial permanent disability and that the minor petitioner is entitled to Rs.3,000/- for every percentage of disability.

Accordingly, awarded a sum of Rs.63,000/- under the head 'partial permanent disability' and also awarded compensation under various other heads as Minor M. Arun S/O.N.Moorthy vs The Managing Director on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72648570/

6.Not being satisfied with the Award passed by the Tribunal, the petitioner has preferred this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal.

Arguments 7.The learned Counsel for the appellant / petitioner has submitted that though the Medical Board observed the injury suffered by the petitioner on his right leg middle toe, it failed to assess the disability suffered by the petitioner on that account.
The injuries on the right leg middle toe and the left leg have rendered the petitioner unable to stand for long periods, walk, squat or sit cross-legged.
He is unable to perform his day-to-day activities independently as before the accident.
Further, the Medical Board has failed to https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2344 OF 2022 assess whole body disability.
Due to the accident, the petitioner has lost his amenities.
Petitioner underwent immense pain, sufferings, and mental trauma at such a tender age due to the accident.
The Tribunal without properly appreciating the facts and circumstances of the case, awarded a meagre compensation.
Accordingly, she prayed to enhance the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
7.1.In support of her submission
, learned counsel for the appellant / petitioner relied on the following judgments:

(i)Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager,
National Insurance Company Limited and Another [2014 (14) SCC 396]
(ii)Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kumari Kiran Through Her Father Harinarayan Vs. Sajjan Singh and Others [2015 (1) SCC 539]
(iii)Judgment of this Court in Minor Aravinth Vs. Murali Transports and Another [CMA No.755 of 2018 decided on 17.02.2022]
(iv)Division Bench Judgment of this Court in M/s.IFFCO TOKIO General Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Minor. S.Vijay Sai and Another [CMA Nos.573 and 576 of 2020 decided on 07.07.2022] https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2344 OF 2022 8.Per contra, the learned Counsel for the respondent has submitted that no serious injuries were caused to the appellant / petitioner as alleged.

sentences.text: The Tribunal, after considering Ex-C.1 - Disability Certificate and Ex-P.3 - Discharge Summary, has rightly awarded compensation to the appellant / petitioner.
Hence, there is no warrant to interfere with the Award passed by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, he prayed to dismiss the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal.
Discussion and Decision
9.This
Court has considered the submissions made on either side and perused the case papers.

10. As far as negligence is concerned, the Tribunal, based on the evidence of P.W.1, Ex-P.1 - FIR and Ex-P.7 - Charge Sheet, concluded that the Driver of the respondents Bus is responsible for the accident.
This Court has no reason to deviate from the said finding.
Accordingly, this Court concurs with the said Tribunal's finding.

Moreover, the appellant / petitioner has filed this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal seeking enhancement of compensation and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2344 OF 2022 the respondent has not filed any appeal / cross objection.
Hence, the only point of contention is the quantum of compensation and there is no need to narrate the facts pertaining to the manner of accident.
11.Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was admitted to Government Hospital, Kurinjipadi and later, on the same day, transferred to Government Headquarters Hospital, Cuddalore.

Thereafter, he was admitted in Mahatma Gandhi Medical College and Research Institute,
Pondicherry on October 10, 2014, doctors whereof diagnosed that the petitioner suffered UNDISPLACED SUPRACONDYLAR # LEFT FEMUR WITH UNDISPLACED # BASE OF RIGHT 3RD METATARSAL vide Ex-P.3 - Discharge Summary and opined that the petitioner suffered grievous injuries vide Ex-P.2 - Accident Register.

entities.text:
Mahatma Gandhi Medical College and Research Institute,
Pondicherry
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner was discharged from the said Hospital on October 20, 2014.
The petitioner marked Ex-P.4  Medical Bills which shows that he incurred a sum of Rs.6,076/- towards medical expenses.
12.The

Medical Board examined the petitioner and issued Disability Certificate (Ex-C.1), wherein,
the Medical Board has noted an injury on the petitioners left leg as well as another injury on the petitioners right leg middle toe.
However, the Medical Board certified that the petitioner https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2344 OF 2022 suffers 21% permanent disability in respect of his left leg alone.
It is unfortunate that Ex-C.1 is silent about the disability suffered by the petitioner on account of the injury on the right leg middle toe as well as the whole-body disability or lack thereof.
This discrepancy underscores the need for the Medical Board to take a more thorough and serious approach towards medical assessments.
13.Ex-P.3 is the discharge summary issued by the Department of Orthopedic Surgery, Mahatma Gandhi Medical College and Research Institute, Pondicherry.

14.The

Tribunal held that the petitioner did not suffer any permanent disability but only 21% partial permanent disability and thus, by fixing a sum of Rs.3,000/- for every percentage of disability,
arrived at a compensation of Rs.63,000/- under the head 'partial permanent disability'.

For this finding, the Tribunal relied on the following portion of Ex-P.3:
Course in Hospital:
Patient was admitted for the above complaints.
All basic investigations were done and found to be under normal limits.
Left A/K Slab, Right B/K slab applied on 10.10.2014.
Left A/K cast conversion done on 18.10.2014.
The patients condition clinically improved and hence discharged on 20.10.2014.
(emphasis supplied by this Court)
said approach of the Tribunal, in the opinion of this Court, is misconceived.

Comprehensive reading of Ex-P.3 would clearly show that by the words All basic investigations were done and found to be under normal limits, the author of Ex-P.3 was referring to the results of the laboratorial examinations such as pathological and microbiological https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2344 OF 2022 examinations done on the petitioner.
Ex-C.1 - Disability Certificate and Ex- P.2 - Accident Register also do not support the interpretation of the Tribunal.
Further, the very fact that the author has employed the terms basic investigations and under normal limits shows that the author was referring to laboratorial examinations.
Hence, the finding of the Tribunal that the petitioner does not suffer any permanent disability, but only partial permanent disability is incorrect and therefore, liable to be set aside.

15.At this Juncture, it is apposite to cite the Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited and Another [2014 (14) SCC 396]
relied on by the learned Counsel for the appellant, wherein guidelines regarding the assessment of compensation in case of minor victims of motor vehicle accident have been laid down.

entities.text: Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited and Another [2014 (14) SCC 396]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In Paragraph No.12 of the Judgment, it is held thus:
12.Though it is difficult to have an accurate assessment of the compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of a motor vehicle accident, having regard to the relevant factors, precedents and the approach of various High Courts,
we https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2344 OF 2022 are of the view that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc., should be, if the disability is above 10% and upto 30% to Minor M. Arun S/O.N.Moorthy vs The Managing Director on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72648570/
5
the whole body, Rs.3 lakhs; upto 60%, Rs.4 lakhs; upto 90%, Rs.5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be Rs.6 lakhs.
For permanent disability upto 10%, it should be Re.1 lakh, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take different yardstick.
(emphasis supplied by this Court)
15.1.To be noted, in the above case, the petitioner therein suffered 34% disability of right lower limb and 18% to the whole body.

16.Further, in the Judgment of this Court in Minor Aravinth's case (cited supra)
relied on by the learned Counsel for the appellant / petitioner, the accident had occurred on March 12, 2005, and the victim was four years old at the time of accident.
Due to the accident, the minor child was completely disabled and could not continue schooling, and he was continuing treatment even at the time of filing of petition before the Tribunal.

Considering the facts and circumstances of that case, learned Single Judge of this Court by following the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mallikarjun's case (cited supra) awarded a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- towards https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2344 OF 2022 whole body disability to the minor appellant therein.
17.There is no quarrel with the legal proposition put-forth / followed in the aforementioned Judgments.
But in the instant case, the Medical Board has failed to consider the injury on the right leg middle toe while assessing permanent disability.
It fails to assess the whole-body permanent disability of the petitioner or lack thereof as well.

18.Given the facts and circumstances of the case, in the interest of justice and also considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, period of treatment viz., 11 days, Ex-P.2 - Accident Register, Ex-P.3 - Discharge Summary, the fact that the Medical Board assessed that the petitioner suffers 21%
permanent disability in respect of his left leg vide Ex- C.1, this Court is of the considered view that the appellant / petitioner would have suffered whole body permanent disability of not more than 10%.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head Permanent Disability as per Mallikarjun's case (cited supra).
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2344 OF 2022
19.The

Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards pain, sufferings and mental agony, which,
in the considered opinion of this Court is on the lower side and this Court is inclined to enhance the same to Rs.50,000/- considering the tender age of the petitioner and the injuries sustained by him.
20.The
Tribunal awarded a sum Rs.4,500/- towards attender charges; Rs.5,000/- towards transportation to hospital; and Rs.6,076/- towards medical bills.

This Court is of the view that the Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation under the above heads and hence, there is no warrant to interfere with the same.

sentences.text: Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.4,500/- towards extra nourishment.
Considering the nature of the injuries, the period of treatment undertaken and the age of the petitioner, awarding a sum of Rs.10,000/- under the head 'extra nourishment' would be fair and just.
Accordingly, this Court is inclined to enhance the same to Rs.10,000/-.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA NO.2344 OF 2022
22.Due to the accident, the petitioner has lost amenities to some extent.
The petitioner cannot be physically active as others of his age or as he was before, and also cannot effectively participate in sports and other school activities.
Hence, this Court is of the view that the Tribunal ought to have awarded compensation under the head loss of amenities.
The Tribunal failed to do so.

Hence, this Court is inclined to award a sum of Rs.25,000/- under the head 'loss of amenities'.
23.Accordingly
, the petitioner is entitled to get enhanced compensation of Rs.2,00,576/- (Rupees Two Lakh Five Hundred and Seventy Six only) from the respondent as tabulated hereunder:

, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal viz., Rs.1,13,076/- is hereby enhanced to Rs.2,00,576/- (Rupees Two Lakh Five Hundred and Seventy Six only).
